title: Traction Drive: Motor Controllers, Motors and Gearboxes

blocks.text: Shaddad is a skid-steer vehicle, so it has two independent traction drives, one per track. Each drive has a commercial-class field-oriented motor controller (ESC), a 48 V surface PMSM, a two-stage 24:1 planetary gearbox, a spring-applied brake on the motor shaft, and a thermal network for the winding, housing and ESC heat sink. The STM32H743 MCU never runs field-oriented control. Every 10 ms it sends a speed setpoint, a torque feed-forward and two torque limits on CAN1. The ESC closes the speed loop at 1 kHz and returns its state, measurements and available torque. Phase 1 (RC) and Phase 2 (autonomy) use this interface unchanged.

This chapter explains the drive model one side at a time. It covers the ESC firmware model, the motor plant variants, the gearbox, brake and thermal network, and the CAN codecs. It also describes the integration defect that kept the robot from moving in the first system run, and the verification evidence. All drive `.slx` files are generated by `scripts/build/build_drive.m`, and the test benches by `tests/drive/build_tb_drive.m`. The state-machine function `esc_sm.m` is hand-written. All parameters come from `params/param_drive.m`, which `shaddad_params` assembles as `P.drive`.

blocks.text: In `drive_system`, `drive_cmd_unpack` decodes the DRV_CMD frame at 10 ms, and a Rate Transition re-times the command to 1 ms. Inside `drive_side` ({fig:F07_drive_side_overview.png} and {fig:F07_drive_side_detail.png}; the numbers in parentheses are the callouts) the command enters `drive_esc` (1). The ESC output `plant_cmd = [Tr; brake duty; w_cmd; enable]` leaves the ESC output stage through a 1 ms Unit Delay (decision D36, a modelled ESC compute delay that also breaks the algebraic loop). It then drives the selected motor plant (2). The motor shaft connects to the gearbox input (3) and to the brake (4). The gearbox output is the physical port `Spr`, which `drive_system` exposes as `Spr_L`/`Spr_R` and wires to the track sprockets in the structure plant. The DC ports `DC48_TracL/R_p/n` connect to the fused 48 V traction feeds of `Power_Plant`. The measured motor angle, DC voltage, DC current, winding temperature and heat-sink temperature return to the ESC through deterministic 1 ms Rate Transitions (6). The ESC derives motor speed from the quantised angle. Motor speed, torque and housing temperature go to the truth bus (9) only, together with the power products and energy integrals (8). The drive files contain no Solver Configuration and no Electrical Reference (D15). The Solver Configuration sits at the `Shaddad_Plant` top level on `DC48_TracL_n`, and the single Electrical Reference is inside `Power_Plant/PDU`.

blocks.text: Sizing and Design Values

The drive spec sizes the drive for a 600 kg design mass (450 kg curb plus a 150 kg implement), a 0.85 m track gauge, a 1.0 m contact length and a 0.128 m sprocket pitch radius. The current model weighs 469 kg at curb and 609 kg with a full sprayer, which is close to the design point. {tab:tab_drive_loads} lists the load cases and also shows the check at 609 kg. Sprocket torque is F x r_s. Motor torque is the sprocket torque divided by N x eta = 24 x 0.94 = 22.56.

blocks.text: The design points are F_peak = 2100 N, which is traction-limited, and F_cont = 1000 N. They need 11.9 N m peak and 5.7 N m continuous at the motor. The motor is rated **16 N m peak (30 s) and 8.0 N m continuous**. The 20° climb (7.0 N m) therefore fits inside the continuous rating. The pivot turn uses 61 % of peak torque. The gear ratio comes from speed. The manual speed limit is 2.0 m/s, and the design maximum track speed is 2.2 m/s (outer track in a turn). That is 17.2 rad/s (164 rpm) at the sprocket, and a usable motor top speed of about 4000 rpm gives N = 24. The track-to-motor speed factor is `P.drive.gear.k_v2w` = N/r_s = 187.5 (rad/s)/(m/s), so 2.0 m/s is 3581 rpm and 2.2 m/s is 3939 rpm. Both are below the 4500 rpm maximum and the 4800 rpm overspeed trip. At 2 m/s and 6.8 N m the motor needs at least 39.4 V DC. The 16S LiFePO4 pack covers that over its whole 40-58.4 V range, and the voltage-dependent torque envelope models the loss of top speed at low state of charge. {tab:tab_drive_design} summarises the main design values.

blocks.text: ESC Firmware Model (drive_esc)

`drive_esc` is a behavioural model of a commercial CiA-402-class traction controller. Everything in it runs at `P.drive.Ts_esc` = 1 ms. It uses library blocks only, except the state machine. Stateflow is not installed (decision D1), so the state machine is a MATLAB Function block that calls `esc_sm.m` with persistent state and the enumeration `EscState`. The function is an ordered transition table, so it maps one-to-one onto a Stateflow chart if Stateflow is installed later. {fig:F08_drive_esc_overview.png} shows the top level, {tab:tab_esc_subsys} lists the subsystems with their callout numbers, and {fig:F08_drive_esc_detail.png} shows the control path at a readable scale.

blocks.text: State Machine

The states follow the CiA 402 power-drive state machine: not ready, ready, operation enabled, quick stop and fault. Timers count 1 ms ticks. The thresholds are in `P.drive.sm`. {tab:tab_esc_states} lists the states.

blocks.caption: ESC_SM states (EscState, sent as uint8 in DRV_FB3)
rows: enable, mode SPEED or TORQUE, no park_req, no CAN timeout: ENABLING
!enable or park_req: DISABLING; CAN timeout: QUICK_STOP
engaged after abs(w) < 2 rad/s for 0.2 s
80 ms after engaging: READY; enable again: OPERATION/ENABLING
fault_reset edge, no hard fault: READY

items: **Priority:** STO, then hard fault, then undervoltage (`v_dc < V_off` = 35 V gives NOT_READY), then CAN timeout, then operator commands. A hard fault is any fault bit except UNDERVOLTAGE, CAN_TIMEOUT and STO_ACTIVE (`P.drive.sm.hard_mask`).

**PARKED substate:** in OPERATION, when the command is zero (abs(w_ref) < 0.05 rad/s) and abs(w) < 2 rad/s for 2 s, the brake engages and torque goes off 80 ms later. A non-zero command returns the ESC to ENABLING. The robot therefore holds on a slope without current.
**Brake driver:** the coil gets full duty for a 0.2 s pull-in and 48 % hold duty after that. Zero duty means the spring is applied, so the brake fails safe.
**Always-on logic:** the ESC logic stays powered when the DC link is dead, so feedback frames continue in NOT_READY. The MCU can then tell a dead link from a lost ESC.

**Parameter path:** `P.drive.sm_vec` reaches the MATLAB Function through a Constant block, not as parameter data. `drive_esc` sits three Subsystem Reference levels deep, and at that depth parameter data occasionally triggers the R2026b JIT relink assertion `o != nullptr`.

blocks.text: Speed Loop, Ramp and Feed-Forward

`Speed_Ctrl` sets the target to zero in the hold-zero states (ENABLING, DISABLING, QUICK_STOP, PARKED) and to `w_ref` otherwise. A Rate Limiter Dynamic limits the target to ±420 rad/s² (2.24 m/s² at the track), or ±375 rad/s² (2.0 m/s²) in QUICK_STOP. While the loop is inactive the ramp follows the measured speed, so the next enable starts without a bump. Under decision D33 the MCU shaper is the only deceleration limiter. `shaddad_params` asserts that the ESC ramp is above every MCU deceleration profile.

The speed controller is a Discrete PID Controller in parallel PI form. It uses **Kp_w = 0.13 N m/(rad/s)** and **Ki_w = 0.39 N m/rad** with Backward Euler integration. Its external saturation limits are the torque-limiter bounds minus the feed-forward, so PI plus feed-forward never leaves the limits, and clamping anti-windup is on. The integrator resets whenever the loop is inactive. In SPEED mode the torque command is PI plus feed-forward. In TORQUE mode `tau_ff` is the setpoint. The result is clamped to `[lo, up]`, multiplied by the fault-injection factor `tau_scale`, and gated by `torque_en`. The MCU sends `tau_ff = Kff_a x a_track_ref`. In the hold-zero states, where the MCU sends no feed-forward, the ESC adds its own inertia feed-forward `J_ff x d(w_ramp)/dt` with J_ff = 0.0102 kg m² (rotor plus 300 kg reflected). Without it, the stop with the low D50 gains would lag and overshoot.

Decision D50 tuned the gains on a two-mass model. One mass is the belt side (motor, gearbox, sprocket and belt, 2.583e-3 kg m² at the motor). The other is the vehicle half-mass behind the track shear spring. The model includes a 5 ms torque lag, a 2 ms speed filter and a 2.5 ms delay. The rigid design gives a 14.3 rad/s crossover with 70° phase margin. Across farm, sand, wet and asphalt soils at 469 and 609 kg it keeps PM ≥ 63°, GM ≥ 14.6 dB, Ms ≤ 1.43 and closed-loop damping ≥ 0.43. The revision-A gains (0.255 / 1.59) reached only PM 41°, Ms 2.04 and damping 0.19 once track compliance was included.
Torque Limiter and tau_avail

The limiter combines the peak envelope, an I2t boost budget, thermal and voltage derating, the DC current limits and the MCU's commanded limits. It selects the limits by quadrant, so motoring and regeneration are limited separately. The implemented law (`drive_esc/Torque_Limiter`) is:

tau_env  = EnvPeak(|n| [rpm], v_dc)          % 2-D LUT P.drive.motor.T_pk_2D (same table as the plant)
tau_cont = EnvCont(|n| [rpm])                % 1-D LUT P.drive.motor.T_cont_nom
r        = (|tau_applied| / max(tau_cont, 0.5))^2
dx/dt    = (r - 1)/k_boost   if r > 1        % k_boost = ((16/8)^2 - 1) * 30 s = 90 s: 30 s at 16 N m
         = (r - 1)/t_recover otherwise        % t_recover = 60 s;  x limited to [0, 1]
exhausted = Relay(x; on 1 - 1e-6, off 0.01);  tau_I2t = exhausted ? tau_cont : tau_env
f_Tm = LUT(T_mot_meas: 413.15 -> 438.15 K = 1 -> 0)   f_Te = LUT(T_esc: 358.15 -> 373.15 K = 1 -> 0)
f_uv = LUT(v_dc: 38 -> 42 V = 0 -> 1)                 f_ov = LUT(v_dc: 57 -> 60 V = 1 -> 0)
TauThMot = tau_I2t * f_Tm * f_Te * f_uv              TauThReg = tau_I2t * f_Tm * f_Te * f_ov
TauDcm   = 100 A * v_dc / max(|w|, 50 rad/s)         TauDcr   = 40 A * v_dc / max(|w|, 50 rad/s)
TauMot   = min(tau_lim_mot, TauThMot, TauDcm)        TauReg   = min(tau_lim_reg, TauThReg, TauDcr)
up = (w <= -5 rad/s) ? TauReg : TauMot               lo = (w >= 5 rad/s) ? -TauReg : -TauMot
tau_avail = min(TauThMot, TauDcm)                    % ESC capability in DRV_FB2 (fix 2026-10-23)

The I2t integrator uses the torque actually applied, after the 1 ms delay. The relay off point is `P.drive.esc.x_off` = 0.01, not the 0.8 in drive spec 6.4. With 0.8, peak torque returned after only 12 s of zero torque, which contradicts spec test T4 (about 60 s). The `DERATING` status bit is set when the boost budget is exhausted or the product of the thermal and undervoltage factors drops below 0.999. `tau_avail` is the motoring torque the ESC itself can deliver now. It deliberately leaves out the MCU's own `tau_lim_mot`. The section on the deadlock below explains why.

blocks.text: Protection Relay blocks (`mcblib`) latch the faults, and the `fault_reset` rising edge clears them. The status word carries b0 READY (states 2-6), b1 OP_ENABLED, b2 FAULT, b3 DERATING, b4 BRAKE_RELEASED, b5 MODE_SPEED, b6 MODE_TORQUE, b7 TORQUE_LIMIT_ACTIVE, b8 STO_ACTIVE, b9 QUICKSTOP and b10 STALL_WARNING. The hardwired `sto_ok` signal from the safety chain bypasses CAN. When it is low the state machine goes to STO in the same 1 ms sample, and the torque command reaching the plant is zero one sample later.
Undervoltage Logic and the E-Stop Restart Fix

A hardware E-stop opens STO first. The safety chain then opens the K1/K2 contactors, and the ESC DC links decay below 35 V. In revision B, undervoltage was armed for good after the first time v_dc exceeded V_on. Both ESCs therefore latched UNDERVOLTAGE during every E-stop, and the MCU treated this as a drive fault (DRV_L/R_FAULT). After the E-stop was released and reset, the robot did not restart (scenario S8a failed). Revision C, applied on 2026-10-23, follows DS402 semantics. A dead DC link while the power stage is off only means not ready to switch on, which is not a fault:

armed(k) = pwr_en(k-1) OR (armed(k-1) AND v_dc(k) < V_on)   % pwr_en: torque_en, 1 ms delay
UV relay input = armed ? v_dc : V_nom                       % not armed: the relay never counts

The hold term keeps the relay counting through its 50 ms debounce after `ESC_SM` has already dropped to NOT_READY at V_off. A DC-link collapse during operation is therefore still a latched fault (test T11). In INIT, NOT_READY, READY, STO, FAULT and PARKED a dead link no longer latches UNDERVOLTAGE. From READY or PARKED the ESC drops to NOT_READY and returns to READY by itself when HV comes back. An ESC in STO or FAULT leaves those states only when `sto_ok` returns or on a fault-reset edge, as before. The fix pass added the bench test T24 for this case, but no run of it is recorded yet. The system scenario S8a (PASS 6/6) verifies the change. In S8a the robot stops 0.213 m after the front E-stop at 1.19 m/s and resumes 1.19 m/s after reset and re-arm.
Motor Plant Variants

`drive_side` holds the motor plant in a Variant Subsystem controlled by `VC_DRIVE_FID`, with activation time `update diagram` because it contains Simscape blocks. The Variant Subsystem has two choices, SYS (`VC_DRIVE_FID == 1`) and IDEAL (`VC_DRIVE_FID == 3`), with identical ports: `cmd = [Tr; duty; w_cmd; en]` in, `meas = [theta_m; w_m; tau_m; v_dc; i_dc]` out, the DC pair, the motor shaft, and the thermal port H. The ports must match because every choice has to belong to the single DC48 Simscape network (D35). The FOC plant `drive_plant_foc` has the same ports but is not a choice. The bench `tb_drive_foc` builds its own copy of the `drive_side` contents with `drive_plant_foc` in place of the Variant Subsystem (`build_drive('side_foc_body', target)`). The value `VC_DRIVE_FID = 2` is reserved and rejected. {tab:tab_drive_fid} compares the three fidelity levels.

blocks.text: **SYS** is the default (`P.drive.fidelity` = 1). The Simscape Electrical block takes the torque reference and applies the voltage-dependent peak envelope `T_pk_2D` (16 N m up to 2500 rpm at 51.2 V, then constant power to 4000 rpm, zero at 4800 rpm). It draws DC power `T w + P_loss(w, T, T_w)` from the link. The loss map `P_loss = P_cu + P_fe + P_esc` is generated offline by `param_drive.m` from copper loss with a temperature coefficient, hysteresis and eddy-current iron loss, and ESC conduction and switching loss. It gives 92.8 % motor-plus-ESC efficiency at 3000 rpm and 8 N m (25 °C). The plant also contains the ESC DC link (2.2 mF with 10 mΩ ESR), an 8 W quiescent load (328 Ω), a 10 kΩ bleed resistor and the brake coil as a Variable Resistor `R_coil/max(duty, 1e-4)`. The block enable input is driven by `1 - enable`, so no DC power is drawn with the inverter off. An open contactor therefore cannot pull the DC link below zero (spec risk R6). The block puts its whole loss into port H, which is the winding node. Rotor-damping heat and DC-harness heat are returned to the thermal reference, so the winding sees only `P_loss`.

**FOC** is bench-only (D52). Its 1e-4 s and 5e-5 s rates are outside the system rate set, and `shaddad_params` rejects `VC_DRIVE_FID = 2`. The current controller uses pole-zero cancellation with a 500 Hz bandwidth (Kp = Lq x 2 pi x 500 = 0.25 V/A, Ki = Rs x 2 pi x 500 = 25 V/(A s)), d-q decoupling feed-forward and min-max zero-sequence injection. **IDEAL** has about two states per side instead of about eight.

IDEAL is a speed source. It ignores the torque command, so the torque limiter, torque saturation on slopes or in pivot turns, and the brake-hold physics have no effect on the motion. Use IDEAL only where torque-level behaviour does not matter. The Phase 1 scenarios in this report run with SYS (the default).
Gearbox, Brake and Thermal Network
Gearbox

`drive_gearbox` uses the foundation `Gear Box` with N = 24 (port B on the motor side, F on the sprocket side). The load-dependent mesh loss uses standard blocks only. An Ideal Torque Sensor measures the output torque, and an Ideal Torque Source applies `T_loss = -k_loss x |T_out| x tanh(w_out/0.5 rad/s)` with k_loss = (1 - 0.94)/0.94 = 0.0638. That gives 94 % efficiency in both power directions. A Rotational Friction element at the input models no-load drag (0.10 N m breakaway, 0.08 N m Coulomb, 1.6e-4 N m s/rad viscous; about 38 W at 3000 rpm). An Inertia models the output carrier (0.02 kg m²). Backlash (15 arcmin) is not modelled. Under D51 the rating is T2N 280 N m (above the pivot load of 222 N m and the adhesion limit of 264 N m), T2B 380 N m (above 16 x 24 x 0.94 = 361 N m) and T2NOT 560 N m. `shaddad_params` asserts that the motor peak through the gear stays below T2B. At standstill the smooth loss law is zero, so a locked sprocket at 16 N m sees the full 384 N m. That is below T2NOT.
Spring Brake

`drive_brake` connects a `Rotational Friction (AB)` with variable normal force to the motor shaft through `Interface (AB-Rotational)`. The housing is a `Rotational World (AB)`. The normal force is `N = 375 N x (1 - f_rel)` with r_eff 0.08 m, static friction 0.40 and Coulomb friction 0.333. That gives 12 N m static and 10 N m dynamic torque, or 288 N m holding torque at the sprocket. The release fraction `f_rel` follows the energised coil through a Rate Limiter (40 ms release, 60 ms engage). The `brake_stuck` injection forces `f_rel = 0`. The smooth friction law causes a small creep of about 0.02 m/h at the track on a 20° slope. This is a modelling artefact, inside the 0.05 m/h limit of test T8.

blocks.text: At the rated point (3000 rpm, 8 N m) and 40 °C ambient, the network settles at about 129 °C winding temperature (class H). At 50 °C ambient with solar load, derating starts after about 35 min at full rated load. Typical field duty of 3-4 N m stays below 100 °C. The ESC reports the derated capability through `tau_avail`, so the MCU and GNC can plan with it.
CAN Codecs: DRV_CMD and DRV_FB

The drive protocol runs on CAN1: classic CAN 2.0B, 500 kbit/s, 11-bit identifiers, little-endian, with node IDs 1 (left) and 2 (right). The codecs are built from `Byte Pack`/`Byte Unpack` (`byteAlign` 1) and bit-field blocks, and use single and integer types only. The four codec files are shared between the two ends. `drive_system` uses `drive_cmd_unpack` and `drive_fb_pack`. The MCU codec `fw_can1_codec` uses `drive_cmd_pack` and `drive_fb_unpack`. It sits at the `Shaddad_MCU` top level, outside the `IO_In`/`IO_Out` variants, so it serves both the SIM and the HW (STM32 FDCAN) IO variants. {tab:tab_drv_frames} lists the DRV frames.

items: **Invalid frame = hold last:** `drive_cmd_unpack` and `drive_fb_unpack` ignore a frame that is not valid or has another ID, and hold the previous payload.
**Timeouts:** the ESC enters QUICK_STOP after 100 ms without an `alive` change (10 missed frames). The MCU decoder clears `rx_ok` when FB1 or FB3 is older than 5 frames (50 ms).
**Frame drops:** losing single frames does not trip the watchdog. At 10 % random drops (T18) the longest run was 2 frames, with no timeout.
**MCU side:** `fw_vehicle_ctrl` always sends mode SPEED, `w_ref = k_v2w x v_track_ref`, `park_req = NOT drive_enable` and a free-running 8-bit `alive` counter.

blocks.text: Integration Lesson: The Torque-Availability Deadlock

In the first system acceptance run (2026-10-23), scenario S1 met both RC latency criteria (28 ms and 50 ms), and both ESCs reached OPERATION with speed setpoints of 229 and 221 rad/s. **The robot did not move.** The largest speed magnitude was 7e-17 m/s, and the MCU commanded `tau_lim_mot = 0` on both sides. The drive bench `t_drive` and the MCU control tests were both green.

The cause was a circular minimum across the CAN interface. The MCU computes `tau_lim_mot = min(T_peak, tau_avail, T_pow) x k_tr x k_der` and holds it at 0 while the drive is disabled. The ESC reported `tau_avail = TauMot = min(tau_lim_mot, TauThMot, TauDcm)`, which contains the limit the MCU had just commanded. Both values start at 0, and zero is a fixed point of the loop: each side kept limiting the other to the value it received. The drive bench missed the defect because `tb_drive_profile` commands a constant 16 N m limit. The MCU closed-loop bench `tb_mcu_closed_loop` missed it because its ESC stub returns `tau_avail = T_peak`. Each half was correct against its stub, and the loop existed only in the integrated system.

The fix removes the echo on the ESC side and leaves the MCU limiter unchanged, so the thermal and I2t derating the ESC reports still reaches the MCU. After rebuilding the drive files, S1 passed 12 of 13 criteria in Normal mode; the 13th, the real-time-factor target, is BLOCKED because it needs Accelerator mode.

items: A feedback field must report the producer's own state. It must never echo the consumer's command, or a min/max chain across two components can lock up.
Check any min/max loop that crosses an interface for a zero fixed point, especially where limits are 0 at power-up or while disabled.

A domain bench with a fixed stub cannot find interface loops. At least one closed-loop test must run the real producer and consumer together. Here the system scenario S1 found the defect, not the domain tests.
"ESCs in OPERATION, setpoint non-zero, torque limit zero" is a signature worth monitoring: it appears in the MCU telemetry `tau_lim_mot` and in DRV_FB2 `tau_avail`.

blocks.text: Verification

`tests/drive/t_drive.m` holds the drive acceptance tests: drive spec section 8 (T1-T23, revision B), T24 (added in the fix pass), interfaces, algebraic loops, variants and codecs. It runs on four benches. `tb_drive` is one side with a 51.2 V source plus 20 mΩ, a contactor switch, and either a vehicle load (300 kg as 4.915 kg m² at the sprocket, rolling friction, grade torque) or a dyno. `tb_drive_sys` has both sides. `tb_drive_2mass` has the D50 two-mass load. `tb_drive_foc` uses the FOC plant. The class now has 31 tests, because the fix pass added T24. The last full run, before the fix pass, gave **25 passed, 0 failed, 5 incomplete** out of 30 (`docs/STATUS.md` section 4). The incomplete ones are the T2 spec conflict, the long tests T5, T8 and T17 (which run only with `T06_LONG=1`), and the code-generation check (Simulink Coder not installed). After the fix, T18-T22, the trip test and IDEAL were re-run on the rebuilt `drive_esc` and passed (`work/t06_results.mat`). No run of T24 is recorded. The system scenario S8a checks the same behaviour. {tab:tab_tdrive} lists the result of every test.

blocks.text: **Spec conflict T2.** The overshoot and settling limits were set for the revision-A gains. With the binding D50 gains, the rigid closed-loop pole is at -4.8 rad/s, so no reference weighting can settle to 2 % in under about 0.8 s. The measured unramped step gives 10.2 % overshoot and 0.82 s settling. In operation the MCU shaper and torque feed-forward shape the reference, and D50 predicts less than 0.1 % vehicle-speed overshoot. In the system, S1 measured -0.6 %. **Spec conflict T5.** The spec value of about 20 min for the 63 % rise is a constant-loss estimate (20.3 min at 223 W). With the copper temperature coefficient of the spec loss law, the positive loss-temperature feedback stretches it to 25.3 min, computed with an independent two-node model using the spec parameters. The test bounds the model at ≤ 27 min. Both conflicts are recorded as accepted spec deviations in `docs/STATUS.md`.

System scenarios confirm the drive in closed loop with the MCU, power and structure plants (Normal mode, after the fix pass). In S1 the steady speed error is 0.0072 m/s, the reverse speed error 0.0038 m/s and the stop distance from 1.2 m/s 0.844 m (limit 0.95 m; D33 predicts 0.88 m). The mechanical energy-audit residual is 4.4e-5. In S8a the STO acts 15 ms after the front E-stop, and the robot stops within 0.213 m and restarts after reset. In the D1 default test drive the speed and yaw rate follow the commands within 0.025 m/s and 0.011 rad/s in every segment, with a 25.5 A peak pack current. {fig:F31_drive_internals.png} ({sec:ch03_structure/Structure Signals in the Phase 1 Demonstration}) shows the drive-internal signals of D1: motor speeds up to 2168 rpm, applied motor torques between -5.3 and 4.8 N m, well inside the 16 N m limit, and winding temperatures rising from 45.0 to about 46.2 °C.
Slope Scenario S2

S2 (`scripts/scenarios/scn_S2_slope.m`) is the drive's heaviest Phase 1 case. The `slope_test` world has a 20° ramp along +x from x = 10 m to 30 m with 3 m fillets. The sprayer is fitted with a full tank (`VC_IMPL` 3, 609 kg). The RC throttle commands 0.8 m/s from x = 0 and is released so that the robot stops near mid-ramp. The robot holds there for 30 s (the roll-back criterion checks this hold), then drives on to the plateau (stop time 84 s). S2 was re-run after the fix pass on 2026-10-23 at 20:29 (`work/results/S2_20261023_202915.mat`). For the drive the loads stay well inside the ratings: gearbox torque 221.5 N m peak and 178.5 N m 10 s mean (limits 380 and 280 N m), winding temperature rise 3.9 K, 0.023 m roll-back during the hold and no ESC trip. Three criteria fail (tilt warning, body pitch and mean ground speed on the ramp); {tab:tab_s2_crit} and {fig:F32_s2_slope.png} in {sec:ch09_results/Slope (S2)} give all 11 criteria and the plots.
Working with the Drive Model

Open the project first. `shaddad_startup` then loads `P`, `Ts`, the `VC_*` variables and the buses. Everything below runs in Normal mode, because Windows Application Control blocks Accelerator MEX files on this PC.

items: **Change the model through the scripts.** Every drive `.slx` file is generated, so edit `build_drive.m` (structure) or `param_drive.m` (values) and rebuild. A parameter-only change needs only `shaddad_params()`, because blocks reference `P.drive.*` by name.

**Bench inputs** are model-workspace variables (`tb_cmd`, `tb_load`, `tb_grade`, `tb_Trr`, `tb_vsrc`, `tb_contactor`, `tb_sto`, `tb_w_dyno`). `tb_drive_run` overrides them through `Simulink.SimulationInput` without touching the base workspace.

**Signals:** `so.truth` holds the plant truth (`Bus_DriveSideTruth`: speeds, torques, `tau_brake`, `f_brake_rel`, DC power, temperatures, `E_dc`, `E_spr`, `E_loss`). `so.fb` holds the ESC feedback (`Bus_DriveSideFb`). In system runs both sides appear as `drive_truth.L/R`.

**Fidelity:** a scenario copies every base-workspace `VC_*` variable into its simulation input, so `VC_DRIVE_FID = 3` before a run selects IDEAL. Set it back to 1 afterwards. Value 2 (FOC) is rejected in the system.

blocks.text: The first compile after loading a model with `drive_esc` (three Subsystem Reference levels deep) sometimes stops with the R2026b JIT relink assertion `o != nullptr`. Run the command again; `t_drive` retries once for the same reason.

The ESC model approximates third-party firmware: its speed-loop gains, 5 ms torque lag and motor loss and thermal data are estimates. Once the ESC and motor are chosen, identify them on the bench and update `Kp_w`, `Ki_w`, `Tc` and the loss maps in `param_drive.m`.
